summary: Paul Williams worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, earning his BA from the University of Sussex (~1969–1972) and DPhil from Oxford (~1973–1978). He held posts at Wadham College, Oxford (~1977–1980) and the University of Bristol (~1980–2011).

Paul de Lagarde worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies, studying at Berlin (~1844–1846) under Friedrich Rückert and at Halle-Wittenberg (~1846–1849). He held positions at Halle-Wittenberg (~1851–1852) and the University of Göttingen (~1869–1891).

Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Paula K. R. Arai earned degrees from Kalamazoo College, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University under mentors including Masatoshi Nagatomi. Her academic posts include Vanderbilt University (1994–2002) and Louisiana State University (2007).

Paulinus a Sancto Bartholomaeo worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Charles University, Sapienza University of Rome, and Collegio San Pancrazio. He served in the Malabar Mission (1776–1789) and held posts at the Pontifical Urban University and Congregation of the Index in 1800.

Pe Maung Tin specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from the University of Rangoon, University of Calcutta, and University of Oxford. He served as Professor of Pali and principal at Rangoon, and later led the Burma Historical Commission (1960–1964).
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Sunderland, studying under Peter Harvey.
Pei-jung Wu specializes in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned a BA from National Taiwan University and a PhD from UCLA under doctoral supervisor Donald F. McCallum.

Peipei Qiu works in Japanology and sinology, having studied at Peking University and Columbia University, where Donald Keene served as doctoral supervisor. She held an attested post at Vassar College in 2005.

Pema Bhum specializes in Tibetology and previously served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University Bloomington, as well as director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön works in Buddhist and religious studies, holding degrees from Sarah Lawrence College and UC Berkeley, and studying under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa. She served as director of the Boulder Shambhala Center (~1981–1984) and led Gampo Abbey.
Pema Gyaltsen studied under Palden Sherab and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and taught Rizong Sras Rinpoche.
Pema Kunzang Tendzin studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Pema Namgyel studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, whom he also taught alongside Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Pema Sherpa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, attested as a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University in 2026 under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke.
Pema Tekchok Loden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Thubten Chökyi Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Shenphen Nangwa and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.
Pema Tsewang Gyatso studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.
Pema Vajra 01 studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Patrul Rinpoche, and Thubten Chökyi Dorje, and taught Thubten Chökyi Dorje, Terton Sogyal, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Pema Wangchok Gyelpo worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under masters such as Shenphen Nangwa, Mipam Gyatso, and Khakyab Dorje, and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche, among others.

Penghao Sun works in Tibetology and history and archaeology, having studied under doctoral supervisor Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, as well as teachers including Qingying Chen (2009–2011), Mark Elliott, and Jay Jasanoff.
